parallel.requirements: The parallel attempt recognized the required CLI behavior and reference outputs for default, --a 3, and --a 7, and it identified the task as a small Rust port.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It entered swarm mode but decided no subagent swarm was warranted, retained work in the parent, and then waited for further user instruction instead of continuing.
parallel.implementation: No Rust implementation files were written. The only executed command listed /output and ran the C++ reference binary for three sample inputs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No Cargo project, module file, root test5.rs, executable, or copied artifact was delivered; artifact validation found an empty artifact directory.
parallel.verification: Verification was limited to running the C++ reference executable. There was no Rust compile, cargo build, or Rust output comparison.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: All required deliverables remained missing at closure, so the current official evaluator failed all 39 testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same CLI default, --a count parsing, insertion, even-key erase count, output formatting, Cargo project, root test5.rs, and std-only constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned the whole path from probing through implementation, module organization, local verification, Cargo build, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: It wrote Cargo.toml, src/hopscotch.rs implementing the needed map subset over std::collections::HashMap, and root test5.rs with the CLI and erase logic.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The root binary target referenced the module with an explicit path, compiled to /output/test5, built under Cargo, and artifact validation copied the expected files.
serial.verification: It ran rustc output checks for default and several --a counts, then compared Rust and C++ outputs across seven inputs and ran cargo build --release.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished behavior is visible in the trajectory; official evaluation passed all 39 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received and restated the core task as a small map-count migration but did not act on the project-structure and output-file requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and implemented the required root test5.rs, Cargo project, std-only map behavior, CLI parsing, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized requirements were similar, but serial carried them into implementation while parallel stopped after recognition and probing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel entered swarm mode but created no subagents and the parent chose to wait rather than own the implementation to completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main agent as the complete owner for probing, writing, building, testing, and reporting the solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had continuous single-owner execution; parallel had no executed multi-agent decomposition and abandoned direct ownership before delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child brief, handoff, or cross-agent interface was created; the parent knew the needed CLI behavior from the prompt and reference runs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial encoded the interface locally through Cargo.toml, a root binary path, a module path from test5.rs to src/hopscotch.rs, and std-only implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference is not a cross-agent contract issue: serial built the local file/module interface, while parallel produced no interface or files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel executed only one shell command to inspect /output and run the reference binary for default, --a 3, and --a 7.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the project manifest, a HopscotchMap wrapper module, and the test5.rs binary logic that inserts, erases, and prints the counts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had no Rust implementation path; serial implemented the required behavior in files that the evaluator could build.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results or implementation artifacts to retrieve; the parent closed the turn after a non-delivery response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial write results returned, then compile and comparison results returned before the final delivery message.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial consumed its own write and test results before closure; parallel had no result lifecycle beyond the reference probe and final hold.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel never wrote to the implementation workspace, so there were no shared-state collisions but also no deliverable state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created a coherent local project whose artifact validation included Cargo.toml, test5.rs, src/hopscotch.rs, and built outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's shared state became a buildable project; parallel left the artifact area empty.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified only reference binary outputs and did not compile or run a Rust candidate; official evaluation failed all 39 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran rustc on test5.rs, exercised several Rust outputs, compared seven inputs against the C++ binary, ran cargo build --release, and passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed evaluator-aligned implementation verification; parallel had no candidate to verify.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one Bash call and ended after about 55 seconds without timing out, leaving the task unfinished by choice of closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used three writes and three Bash calls over about 81 agent seconds, still well inside the budget, and closed after delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The failure was not time-budget exhaustion: serial spent more work but completed, while parallel closed early with no artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations are discordant: parallel failed 0/39 while serial passed 39/39. The concrete difference is that the parallel-labeled attempt stopped after reference-output exploration and delivered no files, whereas serial wrote the Cargo project, compiled and tested it, and produced an artifact that the evaluator accepted.
parallel_contributors: The parallel-mode parent treated the small task as not needing a swarm and waited for further instruction instead of implementing the required files.
Artifact validation for the parallel run found an empty artifact directory, leaving the evaluator no test5.rs or Cargo project to build.
serial_contributors: The serial main agent wrote Cargo.toml, src/hopscotch.rs, and root test5.rs in one coherent project.
The serial agent compiled the Rust program, compared outputs against the C++ reference for multiple counts, ran cargo build --release, and passed official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary coding defect explains the parallel failure because the parallel run produced no Rust implementation to inspect.
